title: ZFS/devmapper CoW snapshots for instant cloning
description:
Use copy-on-write snapshots for instant sandbox creation from base images.

Current: Each sandbox copies the full rootfs (~200MB+)
Target: Clone from snapshot in <10ms

Implementation options:
1. ZFS: `zfs clone base@snapshot sandbox-123`
2. devmapper: thin provisioning with snapshots
3. Overlay: overlayfs on top of read-only base

Benefits:
- Instant sandbox creation
- Minimal disk usage (only deltas stored)
- Fast reset to clean state

SlicerVM achieves 280-299ms total boot with CoW storage.

Reference: https://slicervm.com/blog/microvms-sandboxes-in-300ms/

title: Persistent volumes with mount-by-slug
description:
Add persistent volume support that survives sandbox restarts, similar to Deno Sandbox.

## Use Cases

- Cache dependencies between runs (node_modules, pip packages)
- Store datasets for ML training
- SQLite databases that persist
- Shared storage between sandboxes

## API Design

### CLI
```bash
# Create a volume
agentkernel volume create my-data --size 2GB

# Mount in sandbox
agentkernel create my-sandbox --volume my-data:/data

# List volumes
agentkernel volume list

# Delete volume
agentkernel volume delete my-data
```

### SDK (TypeScript)
```typescript
const volume = await agentkernel.volumes.create({
  slug: "training-cache",
  size: "2GB",
});

const sandbox = await agentkernel.create({
  volumes: { "/data": volume.slug },
});

// Files in /data persist after sandbox closes
```

### Config (agentkernel.toml)
```toml
[volumes]
my-data = { size = "2GB", mount = "/data" }
```

## Implementation

1. Store volumes in ~/.agentkernel/volumes/<slug>/
2. Bind mount into container/VM at specified path
3. Track volume metadata (size, created, last_used)
4. Support size limits and cleanup policies

## HTTP API

```
POST /volumes              - Create volume
GET  /volumes              - List volumes  
GET  /volumes/{slug}       - Get volume info
DELETE /volumes/{slug}     - Delete volume
POST /sandboxes            - Accept volumes: {"/path": "slug"}
```

Reference: https://docs.deno.com/examples/volumes_tutorial/
close_reason: Closed

title: Serial Over SSH (SOS) console via VSOCK
description:
Implement SlicerVM-style SOS for console access without SSH/network.

Benefits:
- Available before network is up
- No SSH host key generation delay (saves 200-500ms)
- Works even if network is broken
- Out-of-band debugging

Implementation:
1. VSOCK-based shell server in guest agent
2. Host CLI: `agentkernel console <sandbox>`
3. Direct PTY forwarding over VSOCK
4. No authentication needed (VSOCK is host-only)

```bash
# Instead of waiting for SSH
agentkernel console my-sandbox
# Immediately get root shell
```

title: VSOCK-based secrets injection (SlicerVM pattern)
description:
Implement SlicerVM-style secrets via VSOCK for cases where network-layer injection isn't suitable.

Pattern:
```bash
# Host side
agentkernel secret set OPENAI_API_KEY --value=sk-... --uid=1000 --permissions=0400
agentkernel create my-sandbox --secret=OPENAI_API_KEY

# Inside VM - secrets appear as files
cat /run/agentkernel/secrets/OPENAI_API_KEY
```

Implementation:
1. Secrets stored encrypted on host
2. VSOCK server runs per-VM, serves secrets
3. Guest agent syncs to /run/agentkernel/secrets/
4. File permissions match --uid/--gid/--permissions
5. Secrets can be updated without VM restart

Difference from Gondolin pattern:
- Gondolin: secrets never enter VM (network-layer)
- SlicerVM: secrets enter VM as files (VSOCK-layer)

Both have value - network-layer is more secure, file-layer is more compatible.

Reference: https://docs.slicervm.com/reference/secrets/
close_reason: Implemented in feat/secrets-management branch. Proxy MITM, hooks SDK, file-based secrets, and console all working.

title: Programmable VFS layer (Gondolin pattern)
description:
Add programmable virtual filesystem layer for custom mount backends.

Gondolin uses FUSE with pluggable providers:
- MemoryProvider: in-memory tmpfs
- RealFSProvider: host directory passthrough
- ReadonlyProvider: read-only wrapper
- Custom: remote storage, filtered views

```typescript
const vm = await agentkernel.create({
  vfs: {
    mounts: {
      '/workspace': { type: 'host', path: '/home/user/project', readonly: false },
      '/cache': { type: 'memory', size: '100MB' },
      '/secrets': { type: 'secrets', keys: ['OPENAI_API_KEY'] },
    }
  }
});
```

Use cases:
- Filtered file access (hide sensitive files)
- In-memory scratch space
- Remote storage mounting
- Audit file access

Lower priority since we have mount_cwd already.

Reference: https://github.com/earendil-works/gondolin

title: Custom image builder from Dockerfile
description:
Build custom VM images from Dockerfiles, similar to SlicerVM.

```dockerfile
FROM ghcr.io/thrashr888/agentkernel-base:latest
RUN apk add --no-cache nodejs npm python3
RUN npm install -g typescript
COPY my-tools /usr/local/bin/
```

```bash
agentkernel build -t my-custom-image .
agentkernel create my-sandbox --image my-custom-image
```

Implementation:
1. Use Docker to build the image
2. Extract rootfs from container
3. Package as squashfs or ext4
4. Store in ~/.agentkernel/images/
5. Support pushing to registry

This enables:
- Pre-installed dependencies (faster sandbox startup)
- Custom tools baked in
- Reproducible environments
